title: Play OFC in your browser
summary: Start a hand on your phone and finish it on your computer. Sign in with the same Apple or Google account to see your tables.
notes: Your saved card placements carry over when you switch devices. Table chat and turns update live.

title: More time to read your scoop
summary: The SCOOP! text holds for one second. If a hand ends while you’re away, the celebration plays when you return to its Next hand screen.
notes: Watching or skipping the celebration clears it for that hand.

title: Foul wins get the scoop celebration
summary: Win by foul and you’ll see the SCOOP! animation at showdown.
notes: Heads-up foul wins get the full-screen reveal.
At three-handed tables, the animation plays on the fouled board if it’s the only opponent you scoop. Scoop both opponents for the full-screen reveal.

title: The scoop gets its moment
summary: A gold wipe and a big SCOOP! reveal celebrate winning every comparison at showdown.
notes: At three-handed tables, a single scoop plays inside the swept player’s board so the rest of the table stays visible.
Heads-up scoops and sweeping both opponents get a full-screen reveal.
Reduce Motion keeps the regular score reveal.

title: A better river and faster table switching
summary: River peels, push alerts and table navigation are easier to use.
notes: Tap any unpeeled D5 slot. Opponents see numbered peel progress while unrevealed cards stay private.
Push alerts add chat previews, player names, turn context, Fantasyland card counts and repeat streaks, and final point summaries.
Opening the app clears delivered alerts. Swipe up to dismiss a compact chat banner.
Table swipes wrap in both directions. Ended tables can be archived with a swipe on Play.
Quick heads-up, Friends night and Slow burn are back. Street labels now read Open, D2, D3, D4 and D5.
Fantasyland opening props pay after the natural players finish. When multiple boards are in Fantasyland, the award waits for settlement.
Showdown reveals row scores in stages, emphasizes scoops and swings of at least 30 points, and puts OFC points above props.

title: Restore the current table update
summary: A corrective OTA restored the current table experience on beta and production.
notes: Restored game colors, middle-row bands, river squeeze, discard visibility and the account-level Sweat setting after an older update briefly went out.

title: A stronger, easier-to-grab sweat
summary: The opening-card sweat is easier to hold and gives stronger feedback.
notes: Expanded the touch target, supported two-finger peels and strengthened haptics.
A later update the same day restored the current table release after this older build briefly went out.

title: A middle-row band where scoring differs
summary: The colored band identifies variants where the middle row is scored differently.
notes: Standard High tables no longer show the middle-row band.
Game identity stays visible in the table title.

title: A clearer table for every game
summary: Game colors, river squeeze and showdown details make variants easier to recognize and play.
notes: Each game has a color and a shape cue.
Hold the river cards to squeeze them, or tap for an instant reveal.
See a force-busted player’s discards at showdown.
Sweat the last card is now an account-wide preference.

title: Sweat the last opening card
summary: Peel the last opening card when the first four put you one card away from a first-five prop.
notes: The optional reveal adds suspense while keeping the existing deal and prop results.

title: More ways into Badeucey Fantasyland
summary: Any qualifying 7-high low in the middle now earns Fantasyland.
notes: Older tables and completed hands keep the rules they were dealt with.

title: Swap cards already on your board
summary: Reposition placed cards directly and keep tap placement moving in tray order.
notes: Tap placement advances according to the tray, including in Taiwanese Poker.
Removed the Escalator hint from the table.

title: A quieter table after a quick Set
summary: A fast pre-set no longer leaves a false draft notice behind.
notes: Accepted placements clear the draft feedback when the hand advances.

title: High Pineapple is now labeled High
summary: The app now calls the regular high game “High.”
notes: The label is consistent in setup, the table and the game guide. Existing rules and results carry forward.

title: A smoother table from deal to showdown
summary: A broad pass on cards, table navigation, friends, and accessibility.
notes: Shared motion and haptic feedback make presses, turns, Set and timers feel consistent.
Placed cards travel to their slots. Drag hover highlights illegal rows and snap-back follows the card’s momentum.
Showdown reveals row results in sequence and counts up the score.
Known tables open faster. The deck stays available when switching, and failing polls back off.
Drafts save after a short pause. Play loads cached tables and shows a waiting count on its tab.
Added clearer loading skeletons and Retry actions, instant preference feedback and sign-out confirmation.
Friend actions stay in place, and invitations remember the friend you selected.
Improved autofill, paste, keyboard return keys, larger text, screen-reader labels and contrast.
Close buttons use sheets and back gestures protect multi-step flows.

title: A bigger Fantasyland first five
summary: The first-five reveal uses larger cards and a more prominent Next button.
notes: The reveal is easier to read before you move on to placement.

title: Edit your Dealer’s Choice rotation
summary: Hosts can change the approved game rotation on an existing table.
notes: The table’s next eligible deals use the saved rotation.

title: Table settings and the Fantasyland first five
summary: Review setup choices and see the original five cards in Fantasyland.
notes: The game’s first-five view makes opening-card decisions and props easier to verify.

title: High, Low and Blackjack props
summary: Add optional points-only props to the first five cards.
notes: High, Low and Blackjack evaluate independently, and eligible props can stack.
Opening prop points and regular hand scores remain distinct.

title: Sign in with Google inside the app
summary: Production users on a compatible iPhone runtime can sign in with Google from inside OFC.

title: Bring back 10 on card faces
summary: Ten-rank cards display “10” on their face again.
notes: The card remains the same rank in play and scoring.

title: Table stats and clearer Joker results
summary: See table statistics and Fantasyland frequency, with clearer hand labels when Jokers are used.
notes: Result labels reflect the hand that was actually evaluated.

title: A centered card tray
summary: The fixed tray is centered across the table and the divider is gone.
notes: Tap and drop placement use the same centered layout.

title: Score high-row kickers correctly
summary: High-row foul checks now use the correct kickers.
notes: Opponent result details display the kickers used in evaluation.

title: Steadier tables and wider Fantasyland cards
summary: The board, tray and Set controls stay in stable positions as a hand advances.
notes: Fantasyland uses larger cards across the available width.

title: Untimed by default, with full table settings
summary: New tables start untimed unless you choose a timer.
notes: Creation shows the full settings before you start.
The card tray has a cleaner layout with a full-height Set button.

title: Choose the game and set your cards
summary: The Dealer’s Choice picker closes straight into placement.
notes: Drag and Set the opening hand immediately. The table submits it in the normal turn order.

title: Animated OFC invitations
summary: Shared table links open a short animated OFC preview.
notes: Open in OFC takes the recipient to the invitation in the app.

title: A better Dealer’s Choice and Taiwanese table
summary: The Dealer’s Choice picker fits the current table and Taiwanese hand scores sit inline.
notes: Passive player avatars keep the table focused on play.

title: Dealer’s Choice gets a setup toggle
summary: Choose Dealer’s Choice directly when creating a table.
notes: Select the eligible games before the table is created.

title: A compact Taiwanese table
summary: Taiwanese tables use the shared OFC timer, inline scores and roomier player boards.
notes: The total stays beside your seat and pair scores stay close to the cards.

title: Fixed Fantasyland slots and covered discards
summary: Fantasyland cards stay in their slots while other cards move onto the board.
notes: Discard faces are fully opaque.

title: Keep each Fantasyland card in its slot
summary: Moving a card onto the board preserves the positions of the other cards in the rack.

title: A larger Fantasyland board and a fixed Set button
summary: The board holds its size during placement and Set stays on the right.

title: Drag every card in the Taiwanese rack
summary: Cards throughout the Taiwanese rack can be dragged into place.

title: Steady Fantasyland sizing and quicker Taiwanese Set
summary: Fantasyland keeps the same board size throughout your turn.
notes: Taiwanese gets immediate setting and familiar OFC table controls.

title: Reliable reveal and Set recovery
summary: Recover from interrupted OFC reveals and Set attempts.
notes: Game variants now use one shared lobby experience.

title: Taiwanese Poker comes to OFC
summary: Play Taiwanese Poker with two or three players across four variants.
notes: The release reached the existing beta installer families.

title: Larger, better-aligned opponent boards
summary: Opponent cards grow and align more neatly across the table.

title: Lighter table and chat sync
summary: Reduced unnecessary polling and chat refresh work while keeping tables current.

title: Fit every player on screen
summary: Board layout fits all players more comfortably and completed-hand labels stay visible.

title: Keep cards bright during game selection
summary: Opening cards remain clear when choosing the game at a Dealer’s Choice table.

title: Steadier game selection and optional contacts
summary: Improved Dealer’s Choice selection and the “No Badugi” label.
notes: Compatible beta builds added optional contact discovery.

title: Easier back navigation from practice
summary: Back exits a practice table even when you’re signed out.

title: New card faces and roomier boards
summary: Refreshed card faces, balanced Fantasyland trays and separate three-player boards.

title: A clearer game guide and better next-hand alerts
summary: The guide, action badges, Dealer’s Choice drafts and next-hand notifications are easier to follow.

title: Full boards and a visible Next hand button
summary: Finished boards and Next hand fit together on the results screen.

title: A table dock that stays put
summary: The dock no longer changes height as the available actions change.

title: Tap cards to reveal
summary: Tap opening cards to reveal them. A compact dock leaves more room for the board.

title: Profile photos and full-table swipes
summary: Show a profile photo and swipe across the full table to switch games.

title: Readable tables and Fantasyland selection
summary: Table names are easier to read and Fantasyland selection is clearer in the tray.

title: Switch tables directly
summary: Switch tables with a smoother swipe or jump straight to one using the table picker.

title: More ways to play your turn
summary: Early viewing, presets, table navigation, chat and undo arrived together.
notes: Players can view eligible cards early and use the improved turn controls.

title: An unread dot for table chat
summary: A red dot lets you spot unread table messages before opening chat.

title: Table layout, alerts and draggable sheets
summary: The table is easier to read, notifications are more reliable, and sheets can be dragged.

title: Recover Google sign-in after a callback
summary: A more reliable return from Google sign-in helps the app restore your session.

title: Keep the chosen game through Fantasyland
summary: A Dealer’s Choice hand retains its selected variant through Fantasyland.

title: Show the game preview when your turn starts
summary: The Dealer’s Choice game preview waits for Start your turn.

title: Fix slow table loading
summary: Fixed a push-registration loop that could delay opening a table.

title: Verified iPhone beta update
summary: Verified delivery of the iPhone beta update.

title: A restart prompt that looks like OFC
summary: The update-ready prompt uses OFC’s shared dialog and yellow Restart button.
notes: Includes the reviewed Fantasyland fixes.

title: Restart prompt beta verification
summary: The update-ready prompt was verified across the beta installer families.

title: Restart to apply a downloaded update
summary: OFC now offers Restart when a compatible update is ready to load.

title: The first over-the-air beta
summary: OTA-enabled beta installers can download compatible app updates in the background.
